thread:
emma: Hey — customer upgraded to redwood-py 1.12 and now getting consistent 403s on text.generate. Same code works on 1.11. Also seeing duplicate billing alerts (two charges) for the same request. Any quick repro steps I can give them?

raj: Which call and can you paste minimal repro? SDK version + installed deps also helpful.

emma: Repro steps below that the customer ran locally (they repro reliably):

emma: ```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="sk-live-XXXX")
resp = client.text.generate(model="rwd-small", prompt="hello")
print(resp.text)
```

emma: On 1.11 this returns 200 and content. On 1.12 it raises HTTP 403 from API and logs show no Authorization header on the outgoing request.

tanvi: Interesting — we rolled a change in 1.12 that changed how init kwargs are normalized. If someone passes api_key as a plain kwarg we now expect a credentials object (to support KMS) and we should convert the string into a credential, but a logic path accidentally drops the header when the conversion fails quietly.

raj: That would explain the 403 (missing header). What about the double billing?

billing-bot: Billing team chiming in — duplicate charges usually come from client-side retries resulting in multiple successful requests at the backend. Are they seeing timeouts first?

emma: Customer reports a spike in latency right before the 403s (timeouts), then retries kick in and they get charged twice when one of the retries succeeds.

james: Yep — separate change in 1.12 also modified the retry middleware: we made retry more aggressive and switched from idempotency-aware retries to a simpler at-most-N-retries implementation. For non-idempotent generate calls that can cause duplicate fulfillment if upstream succeeds after a client timeout.

james: TL;DR: two regressions in 1.12: 1) auth header silently dropped for plain api_key string, 2) retries are too aggressive for non-idempotent endpoints.

raj: Workarounds we can give the customer now?

james: Short-term: ask them to pin to 1.11: `pip install redwood==1.11.*` and set env to disable retries for now: `export REDWOOD_CLIENT_RETRIES=0`. That prevents duplicate charges and avoids the auth path that drops the header.

tanvi: For a slightly safer workaround without pinning, they can explicitly pass an Authorization header:

tanvi: ```python
client = RedwoodClient(headers={"Authorization": "Bearer sk-live-XXXX"})
```

emma: I'll pass both options to the customer.

deploy-bot: @james created issue RW-3891 and queued a patch to restore legacy header normalization and revert the retry behavior on canary. Patch id: pr/4582.

james: We'll cut a 1.12.1 hotfix ASAP; ETA a morning patch window. I'll follow up here when it's out.

emma: Thanks — I'll escalate to the account and recommend pinning to 1.11 and the env var header workaround until the hotfix lands.

billing-bot: Noted — billing will watch the account for duplicates and we can refund confirmed duplicate charges after verification.

emma: Closing loop with customer now, will post update when they confirm pin worked.

raj: Thanks, team. Good catch on the two separate regressions.
